subject: Juxtaposing (marginal) prior and posterior in shinyStan

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Juxtaposing (marginal) prior and posterior in shinyStan
parts:
For shinyStan, it would be pretty easy to allow the user to select a prior distribution to add to the posterior density plot for individual parameters so they can view both simultaneously and compare.

Is there any reason not to add this functionality? (The only thing I can think of is that in some cases priors are specified jointly and it might require some work for the user to figure out the marginal prior. But I don't think that's really a reason to avoid offering this.)

Assuming people think this is a good idea, the question is whether to allow the user to input code for a density function or to offer the user a list of choices of distribution families (along with input boxes to enter parameter values). I'm leaning towards the latter option so that we can be sure that it works and people don't spend too much time trying to code their functions properly, etc. The downside to providing a list of choices is that it would be limited to whatever we offer, but I was thinking that, as a start, the following should be sufficient to cover most cases:

normal,
student t,
cauchy,
beta,
gamma (and inverse gamma),
exponential,
chi-sq (and inverse chi-sq)

Are there others that would be essential to include in the first go-around that I'm blanking on?

I've attached two screenshots of this might look like (roughly).

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Juxtaposing (marginal) prior and posterior in shinyStan
parts:
The big problem I see is that it's very error prone
to specify things in two places and try to keep them in
synch. People tend to experiment a lot with models. For
R, you'd need to use our parameterizations to remove the
ambiguity there.

That list doesn't come close to covering the range of
priors people are using for Stan. For example, it doesn't
cover the multivariate cases, pareto, dirichlet, or
uniform, just off the top of my head. There are also all
the issues around applying these to constrained parameters
like simplexes, ordered vectors, Cholesky factors, etc.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Juxtaposing (marginal) prior and posterior in shinyStan
parts:
Bob, I completely agree. I should have said that I was thinking of this particular feature as primarily designed for students. They are typically using less complicated - and primarily univariate - distributions (also not always). I think being able to see the prior and posterior juxtaposed is often very helpful for learning. 

But this raises a more general question that I've been meaning to ask. What's your opinion in general about having features that are only geared toward a subset of users?

And maybe when we start separating prior/likelihood (i.e., base/delta),
then we can do this more automatically.

I'm totally OK with features geared toward a subset of users.
In fact, most features are such when you look at them closely.
